OBJECTIVE OF THE OFFICE/DEPARTMENT

This is a requisition for employment at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)/Regional Office of the World Health Organization (WHO)

Contractual Agreement:

Non-Staff - International PAHO Consultant

Job Posting:

August 21, 2026

Closing Date:

September 20, 2026, 11:59 PM Eastern Time

Primary Location:

Off Site

Organization:

ITS Information Technology Services

Schedule:

Full time

PURPOSE OF CONSULTANCY

This requisition is for a consultancy at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)/Regional Office of the World Health Organization (WHO).
1. Objective of the Department
The Information Technology Services Department (ITS) provides leadership and direction in the deployment of information and communication technologies and systems to support the Pan American Health Organization/Regional Office of the Americas of the World Health Organization (PAHO/WHO) in carrying out its mandate. ITS establishes and maintains strategies, policies, standards, and procedures to ensure the effective and efficient provision of information and communication services in a geographically dispersed environment.

2. Purpose of the Consultancy
PAHO operates Microsoft Fabric as its corporate data and analytics platform. The environment consolidates information from the Organization’s enterprise systems, including the Workday-based PAHO Management Information System (PMIS), corporate applications, and technical data sources, into a common lakehouse and semantic layer that supports institutional reporting, dashboards, and analytical services used by Headquarters, country offices, and centers across the Region of the Americas. Current architecture is built on Azure Data Factory, Azure Data Lake, and SQL Managed Instance architecture, with BI workspaces provisioned in MS Fabric capacities.The platform has grown substantially in scope, data volume, and user base since its adoption, and now underpins reporting relied upon for management and technical decision-making. To sustain this growth and prepare the environment for AI-enabled analytics, PAHO requires an experienced Data, Analytics and AI consultant who can operate the platform on a day-to-day basis while establishing an engineering-grade foundation for its next phase: a complete and maintained architecture and operations baseline, documented platform standards, measurable capacity and cost efficiency, and a progressive Fabric adoption plan with prioritized evolution roadmap for ITS management decision.
This is a hands-on, delivery-focused technical consultancy that combines daily platform operations and support with platform engineering, modernization, and innovation. The consultant will report to the Senior Advisor Applications Development and Support. The consultant will collaborate with ITS units, data and application owners, subject matter experts, and departments across PAHO. The consultant works autonomously against an assigned and prioritized task backlog, delivers within agreed timeframes, and reports formally each month.

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES:

3. Statement of Work

The Data, Analytics and AI consultant will perform the following functions:

3.1 Task Management & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Review the assigned work queue each working day; acknowledge new tasks; confirm scope, priority, acceptance criteria, dependencies, effort, and target completion date.
  • Deliver tasks by the agreed due date. If delivery is at risk, notify the Senior Advisor Applications Development and Support, promptly and propose a recovery plan or revised date for approval.
  • Keep task records current with progress, decisions, blockers, testing evidence, deployment status, and next actions.
  • Work with ITS units, data owners, and PAHO departments to gather requirements, assess impacts, translate needs into feasible solutions, and demonstrate completed work.

3.2 Fabric Platform Operations & Administration

  • Operate and support Fabric capacities, tenant settings, domains, workspaces, gateways and connectivity, OneLake, Lakehouses, Warehouses, SQL endpoints, Data Factory items, notebooks, semantic models and related Power BI services.
  • Monitor capacity utilization, throttling, job concurrency, pipeline and notebook execution, refreshes, query performance, failures, costs and service health; tune or scale workloads within approved limits.
  • Investigate incidents and recurring failures across ingestion, transformation, storage, semantic models, gateways, access and reports; document root cause, corrective action and prevention when required.
  • Maintain schedules, service identities, connections, credentials, operational checks, recovery procedures and support runbooks for production services.
  • Provide level 2/3 support and coordinate with Microsoft, UNICC, vendors and internal teams when an issue requires escalation.
  • Operate and administer the Microsoft Fabric estate on a daily basis, including tenant settings, domains, workspace structures, item lifecycle, licensing assignment, and platform configuration in line with PAHO governance requirements.
  • Manage capacity provisioning, utilization monitoring, throttling and smoothing analysis, workload isolation, and cost optimization on F-SKU capacities using the Fabric Capacity Metrics App; maintain a consumption forecast against contracted entitlement.
  • Monitor and support pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, notebooks, warehouse and lakehouse workloads, and semantic model refreshes; resolve failures, latency, and performance degradation; identify root causes and sustainable corrective actions.
  • Maintain and improve deployment pipelines, workspace Git integration, and environment promotion across development, test, and production.
  • Own backup, resiliency, and recovery for OneLake data and workspace artifacts, including documented and periodically tested recovery procedures for production workloads.
  • Handle incidents, service requests, problems, and changes through PAHO’s corporate IT service management platform, respecting agreed service levels and change control requirements.

3.3 Data Engineering, Integration & Semantic Modeling

  • Design, build, and maintain ingestion and transformation processes using Fabric Data Factory pipelines, Dataflows Gen2, Spark notebooks, shortcuts, and mirroring, applying incremental and cost-efficient patterns.
  • Implement and maintain a medallion (bronze / silver / gold) structure with explicit ownership, contracts, and quality controls between layers.
  • Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations with PAHO corporate systems — in particular the Workday-based PMIS covering human resources, finance, procurement, and grants data — as well as Salesforce, SharePoint, SQL sources, and external data providers, using approved APIs, report-as-a-service extracts, event-driven patterns, and secure authentication mechanisms.
  • Design and maintain dimensional and semantic models (star schema, slowly changing dimensions, Direct Lake), DAX measures, certified datasets, and row-level and object-level security aligned to PAHO’s data access rules.
  • Implement data quality, reconciliation, validation, and lineage controls; investigate and resolve data discrepancies with the relevant data owners and document the outcome.
  • Provide second-level technical support and guidance to PAHO report developers and business power users on modeling, performance, and reporting standards.

3.4 Platform Baseline, Standards & Evolution Roadmap

  • Establish and thereafter maintain a complete and current baseline of the Fabric environment, covering architecture, domain and workspace structure, capacity allocation, data sources and flows, semantic models, security model, integrations, dependencies, operational procedures, and ownership, so that the platform can be operated and handed over by any qualified engineer without reliance on undocumented knowledge.
  • Review the current configuration of capacity, workspaces, pipelines, semantic models, and security against Microsoft reference architecture, well-architected guidance, and PAHO standards; document deviations, risks, technical debt, and remediation options with associated effort and benefit estimates.
  • Identify, quantify, and — once approved — implement optimization opportunities across capacity consumption and cost, refresh and query performance, pipeline design, storage, and licensing.
  • Define, document, and apply platform engineering standards covering naming conventions, workspace and domain strategy, environment separation, source control and CI/CD, promotion and change gates, monitoring and alerting, data quality, and documentation.
  • Produce and maintain a prioritized twelve-to-eighteen-month evolution roadmap for the data and analytics platform, covering architecture, governance, capacity, integration, semantic layer, and AI enablement, sequenced with effort, dependencies, risks, cost implications, and resourcing requirements, for ITS management decision.
  • Provide ITS management with objective, evidence-based analysis of platform health, risk exposure, and improvement priorities on a recurring basis.

3.5 AI-Enabled Analytics & Innovation

  • Assess, pilot, and where approved operationalize Fabric-native AI capabilities, including Copilot in Fabric and Power BI, data agents, AI functions in notebooks, and semantic model preparation for natural-language querying.
  • Build AI-ready data products and semantic layers that can be securely grounded and consumed by PAHO’s Copilot Studio and Power Platform agent portfolio, Azure AI services, and other approved AI solutions.
  • Propose and prototype practical, measurable use cases — such as automated data quality and anomaly detection, forecasting, natural-language reporting, and document or text analytics — presenting expected benefit, consumption impact, and cost before any scaling decision.
  • Apply PAHO’s AI governance, data protection, information classification, and responsible AI requirements; document grounding sources, guardrails, evaluation scenarios, known limitations, and human oversight arrangements.
  • Monitor the Microsoft Fabric and Azure AI roadmap and advise ITS on which capabilities are sufficiently mature for institutional adoption and which should remain experimental, with a clear rationale in each case.

3.6 Security, Governance & Compliance

  • Apply least-privilege access controls across tenant, domain, workspace, item, and data levels, including workspace roles, sharing settings, and conditional access aligned with PAHO requirements.
  • Manage Microsoft Entra ID service principals and app registrations used for Fabric and Power BI automation, including permission scoping, API access configuration, and credential and secret rotation.
  • Administer and validate row-level and object-level security in semantic models, including membership-based security patterns and deployment-time integrity checks.
  • Support Microsoft Purview integration, sensitivity labels, data loss prevention policies, cataloguing, and audit logging in line with approved governance standards.
  • Collaborate with ITS Information Security on reviews, incidents, access recertification, integration dependencies, and remediation activities; do not implement unapproved production changes.

3.7 Documentation, Reporting & Knowledge Transfer

  • Maintain architecture and configuration records, solution designs, data dictionaries, lineage documentation, integration specifications, test evidence, deployment records, runbooks, and task history for all material changes.
  • Store all code, notebooks, pipeline definitions, configuration, documentation, and work products in PAHO-approved repositories, with version control applied.
  • Provide demonstrations, walkthroughs, and structured knowledge-transfer sessions to PAHO staff and authorized support resources, including hands-on enablement on the standards and procedures established.
  • Submit the required monthly activity report and support any ITS reporting requirements toward PAHO management and governance bodies.

4 Monthly Activity Report

By the last working day of each month, the consultant shall submit a consolidated report to the Advisor, IT Operations. The report shall be traceable to the designated task-management system and include:

  • An executive summary and a complete register of every task assigned during the month, plus open tasks carried forward.
  • For each task: identifier, title, requester or owner, assignment date, priority, agreed due date, status, completion date, and task-record reference.
  • For each task: a concise summary of work performed, changes made, testing and approval completed, deployment outcome, documentation produced, and result achieved.
  • For delayed, blocked, cancelled, or re-scoped tasks: reason, impact, required action, mitigation, and approved revised date; plus priorities for the following month.
  • Platform operations for the period: pipeline and semantic model refresh success rates, incidents and problems, production changes and releases, and preventive actions taken.
  • Fabric capacity utilization and consumption against contracted entitlement, with a projection to the end of the contract period, plus cost optimization actions taken or proposed.
  • Progress against the baseline documentation, standards, and evolution roadmap deliverables, including documentation coverage of production workspaces, pipelines, and semantic models.
  • Risks, technical debt, security findings, recommendations, and planned focus for the following month.

A task is considered delivered when deployed to production, verified against the agreed acceptance criteria, documented, and accepted by the requester. Certification of the monthly deliverable is contingent on receipt of a complete monthly report.

5. Qualifications & Skills

5.1 Education & Experience

  • University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Data Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related field from a recognized institution.
  • At least five years of progressively responsible experience in data engineering, analytics, and business intelligence in complex enterprise environments, of which at least three years in a large, multi-location or multi-entity organization.
  • At least two years of hands-on production experience with Microsoft Fabric since its general availability, complemented by prior Power BI Premium and/or Azure Synapse Analytics experience.
  • Demonstrated responsibility for a Microsoft Fabric environment at organizational scale, including capacity administration, domain and workspace design, CI/CD, security, and platform standards, and not solely report or pipeline development.
  • Demonstrated experience documenting, rationalizing, and modernizing an existing analytics environment that has grown organically, including establishing standards and defining a subsequent evolution roadmap adopted by management.
  • Advanced SQL and Python (PySpark); experience with Delta Lake and Parquet; proven experience in dimensional and semantic modeling and advanced DAX.
  • Demonstrated experience integrating enterprise SaaS and ERP systems with analytics platforms using APIs, connectors, and event-driven patterns. Experience integrating Workday (report-as-a-service, Workday APIs, Prism Analytics) with Microsoft Fabric or Azure data platforms is highly desirable.
  • Practical experience with AI-enabled analytics, including Copilot in Fabric or Power BI, data agents, Azure OpenAI, retrieval and embedding pipelines, together with the judgement to assess maturity, cost, and institutional readiness realistically. Highly desirable.
  • Demonstrated ability to work autonomously, manage a prioritized backlog, maintain accurate work records, document rigorously, deliver by agreed deadlines, and communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

5.2 Technical Competencies

Fabric Platform & Administration: Tenant and domain administration, workspace strategy, F-SKU capacity provisioning, Capacity Metrics App, throttling and smoothing analysis, workload isolation, cost optimization, OneLake storage and shortcuts, licensing strategy, on-premises and VNet data gateways, Private Link and managed private endpoints, Admin Monitoring Workspace, backup and disaster recovery for analytics platforms

PURPOSE OF CONSULTANCY

This requisition is for a consultancy at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)/Regional Office of the World Health Organization (WHO).

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES:

1. Objective of the Department

The Information Technology Services Department (ITS) provides leadership and direction in the deployment of information and communication technologies and systems to support the Pan American Health Organization/Regional Office of the Americas of the World Health Organization (PAHO/WHO) in carrying out its mandate. ITS establishes and maintains strategies, policies, standards, and procedures to ensure the effective and efficient provision of information and communication services in a geographically dispersed environment.

2. Purpose of the Consultancy

PAHO operates the Workday-based PAHO Management Information System (PMIS) across human capital management, payroll and absence, finance, procurement, grants, and related processes. The reporting and integration layer delivers operational, managerial, and statutory reporting to business owners and connects Workday to financial, payroll, and identity systems and to the corporate data and analytics platform. ITS seeks a hands-on Workday Reporting and Integrations Consultant to support daily delivery, strengthen reporting and integration reliability, rationalize the report catalogue, and establish practical documentation and development standards. This is a delivery-focused, hands-on technical consultancy.

The consultant reports to and is supervised by the IT Advisor, Business Solutions and Integrations Architect, referred to in this document as the Supervisor, who prioritizes and accepts assigned work. The consultant works within a supported delivery model: business areas approve requirements; the Workday Security team administers security; the PMIS team coordinates releases; and an application management services (AMS) partner provides specialist or overflow capacity. The consultant remains accountable for assigned work and for reviewing AMS work returned within the reporting and integration scope, works autonomously against a prioritized backlog, and reports formally each month.

3. Statement of Work

3.1 Delivery and Stakeholder Coordination

  • Manage an assigned, prioritized backlog; confirm scope, acceptance criteria, dependencies, effort, and target dates; and maintain complete task records in the designated task-management system, which is the source of record.
  • Elicit requirements directly from responsible business areas, translate them into technical specifications, confirm the specification before building, and demonstrate completed work. An incomplete, ambiguous, or technically unachievable specification is returned to the responsible business area and the Supervisor before development proceeds.
  • Coordinate related work with PMIS functional resources, the Workday Security team, and the AMS partner, escalating capacity, capability, access, and critical-path risks through the Supervisor.
  • Notify the Supervisor promptly where delivery is at risk and propose a recovery plan or revised date for approval. Review the existing catalogue before recommending new development and promote reuse over unnecessary custom development.

3.2 Workday Reporting and Data Model

  • Design, build, test, maintain, and optimize Workday reports, particularly Advanced, Matrix, and Composite reports, together with calculated fields, Worksheets, dashboards, discovery boards, and other applicable reporting capabilities.
  • Apply strong knowledge of the Workday data model, including business objects, related business objects, report data sources, indexed data sources, filters, single- and multi-instance relationships, calculated-field dependencies, and relationships between HCM and Financial Management data.
  • Administer report prompts, formatting, sharing, scheduling, delivery, performance, and approved security behavior; tailor delivered reports where appropriate.
  • Maintain the report catalogue and carry out approved ownership, consolidation, rationalization, disablement, and retirement activities under section 3.6.

3.3 Workday Integrations

  • Design, build, test, deploy, and support EIB, Core Connector, Cloud Connect, Document Transformation, RaaS, and REST/SOAP web-service solutions.
  • Develop and troubleshoot XML, XSLT, JSON, transformation logic, integration maps and attributes, launch parameters, transport configuration, PGP settings, and file conventions.
  • Monitor scheduled integrations daily; resolve failures and discrepancies; implement reconciliation, data-quality, root-cause, corrective, and preventive controls; and maintain operational documentation.
  • Specify integration security, credential, key, certificate, and transport requirements and implement integrations within configuration approved and provided by the Workday Security team.
  • Deliver curated Workday data to PAHO’s corporate data and analytics platform through approved extracts, RaaS endpoints, connectors, or web services, ensuring that outputs are reconciled, appropriately secured, efficient, and documented.
  • Migrate reports, integrations, and configuration between tenants using approved promotion procedures.

3.4 Security Operating Model

  • Identify and specify the security needed for assigned reports, data sources, calculated fields, Worksheets, dashboards, and integrations, including least privilege, segregation of duties, ISU/ISSG, domain-access, credential, certificate, key, and transport requirements.
  • Configure integrations to use items approved and issued by the Workday Security team, which retains issuance, custody, and rotation of integration credentials, certificates, and encryption keys. The consultant does not generate, retain, or exchange secret material unless specifically delegated in writing.
  • Do not create, modify, or assign security groups, domain policies, or business-process security policies unless a specific task is explicitly delegated and approved by the Workday Security team.
  • Validate approved security behavior and report access failures, over-permissioning, unintended exposure, expiry risks, or changed data-access requirements promptly.
  • Process PAHO information, including personal, payroll, medical, financial, confidential, or tenant-derived data, only through PAHO-approved platforms. Such information shall not be entered into public or unapproved AI services, and any AI-assisted output used in PAHO work remains subject to consultant review, validation, confidentiality, and human accountability.
  • Maintain audit evidence for report and integration changes, and engage the ITS Information Security unit on security incidents, information classification, credential and certificate handling, and integrations transmitting PAHO data outside the tenant.

  • Provide first-line support for the reporting and integration layer; coordinate Workday Support and AMS cases; and retain responsibility for specification, review, testing, acceptance, and documentation of escalated outcomes.
  • Escalate work to the AMS partner where it exceeds available capacity against agreed priorities, requires capability outside the contracted scope, requires access the consultant does not hold, or is on the critical path for payroll or a financial deadline where reliance on one resource presents unacceptable risk. Escalation outside these criteria requires Supervisor approval.

  • Before proposing retirement, check dashboard and worklet placement, sharing, scheduled delivery, sub-report use, use as another report’s data source, and RaaS or integration consumption. An unresolved dependency prevents retirement.

This is a requisition for employment at the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO)/Regional Office of the World Health Organization (WHO)

Contractual Agreement:

Non-Staff - International PAHO Consultant

Job Posting:

August 20, 2026

Closing Date:

September 20, 2026, 11:59 PM Eastern Time

Primary Location:

Off Site

Organization:

ITS Information Technology Services

Schedule:

Full time

PURPOSE OF CONSULTANCY

The Information Technology Services Department (ITS) provides leadership and direction in the deployment of information and communication technologies and systems to support the Pan American Health Organization/Regional Office of the Americas of the World Health Organization (PAHO/WHO) in carrying out its mandate. ITS establishes and maintains strategies, policies, standards, and procedures to ensure the effective and efficient provision of information and communication services in a geographically dispersed environment.

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES:

2. Purpose of the Consultancy

PAHO has implemented Salesforce Agentforce IT Service as its corporate IT Service Management (ITSM) platform, replacing the legacy service management tool. The platform serves staff members across Headquarters, country offices, and centers in the region of the Americas, and supports other departments beyond ITS.

Following go-live and initial stabilization, PAHO requires an experienced Salesforce Developer consultant to maintain the platform in production and evolve it in line with the Organization’s service management priorities. This is a delivery-focused, hands-on technical consultancy. The consultant will report to the Advisor, IT Operations, and collaborate with other ITS units, service owners, subject matter experts, and departments across PAHO. The consultant works autonomously against an assigned and prioritized task backlog, delivers within agreed timeframes, and reports formally each month.

3. Statement of Work

The Salesforce Developer consultant will perform the following functions:

3.1 Task Management & Stakeholder Coordination

  • Review the assigned work queue each working day; acknowledge new tasks; confirm scope, priority, acceptance criteria, dependencies, effort, and target completion date.
  • Deliver tasks by the agreed due date. If delivery is at risk, notify the Advisor, IT Operations, promptly and propose a recovery plan or revised date for approval.
  • Keep task records current with progress, decisions, blockers, testing evidence, deployment status, and next actions.
  • Work with ITS units and PAHO departments to gather requirements, assess impacts, translate needs into feasible solutions, and demonstrate completed work.

3.2 Salesforce Platform Maintenance, Development & Integration

  • Configure, maintain, and enhance Agentforce IT Service and related Salesforce capabilities supporting incidents, problems, changes, releases, service requests, knowledge, routing, notifications, self-service, and the IT service console.
  • Configure custom objects, fields, page layouts, record types, validation rules, and workflows.
  • Design and deliver maintainable solutions using Salesforce configuration, Flow, Apex, Lightning Web Components, custom metadata, reports, dashboards, and other appropriate platform tools.
  • Develop, maintain, and troubleshoot integrations with PAHO systems using approved APIs, event-driven patterns, middleware, and secure authentication mechanisms.
  • Investigate and resolve issues across configuration, code, automation, data, permissions, integrations, and platform limits; identify root causes and sustainable corrective actions.
  • Support data imports, migrations, cleansing, validation, and quality controls while maintaining integrity and auditability.

3.3 Automation, Agentforce & Knowledge

  • Configure and improve Agentforce agents, topics, instructions, actions, prompt templates, and supporting Flows or Apex components for approved PAHO use cases.
  • Ground AI-enabled experiences in approved PAHO knowledge and data, and work with content owners to improve knowledge quality, relevance, and maintenance.
  • Test agent accuracy, permissions, action execution, human escalation, multilingual behavior where required, and compliance with PAHO privacy, security, and responsible AI requirements.
  • Assess new Salesforce and Agentforce capabilities and recommend practical improvements, recognizing that Agentforce IT Service is a new and evolving product.

3.4 Security, Testing, Release & Production Support

  • Apply least-privilege access controls, secure coding practices, and PAHO security, data protection, change management, and responsible AI requirements.
  • Prepare and execute functional, regression, integration, permission, and agent-behavior tests as applicable; support user acceptance testing and document approval.
  • Manage source-driven changes through approved environments using Salesforce CLI, Git, CI/CD tools, or PAHO's designated process.
  • Prepare deployment, validation, communication, rollback, and post-deployment activities; do not implement unapproved production changes.
  • Provide production support, monitor assigned operational indicators, and prepare root cause analysis and corrective actions when requested.
  • Collaborate with the ITS Information Security and other ITS units on reviews, incidents, access controls, integration dependencies, and remediation activities.
  • Coordinate Salesforce seasonal releases and assess their impact.

3.5 Documentation, Reporting & Knowledge Transfer

  • Maintain solution designs, configuration records, code and integration documentation, test evidence, deployment records, runbooks, and task history for material changes.
  • Document Agentforce configurations, grounding sources, guardrails, evaluation scenarios, known limitations, and operational ownership.
  • Provide demonstrations, walkthroughs, and knowledge-transfer sessions to PAHO staff and authorized support resources.
  • Store all source code, configuration, documentation, and work products in PAHO-approved repositories and submit the required monthly activity report.

4. Monthly Activity Report

By the last working day of each month, the consultant shall submit a consolidated report to the Advisor, IT Operations. The report shall be traceable to the designated task-management system and include:

  • An executive summary and a complete register of every task assigned during the month, plus open tasks carried forward.
  • For each task: identifier, title, requester or owner, assignment date, priority, agreed due date, status, completion date, and task-record reference.
  • For each task: a concise summary of work performed, changes made, testing and approval completed, deployment outcome, documentation produced, and result achieved.
  • For delayed, blocked, cancelled, or re-scoped tasks: reason, impact, required action, mitigation, and approved revised date; plus priorities for the following month.
  • Production releases and incidents in the period, with associated change records and preventive actions taken.
  • Service and agent performance indicators, platform consumption against entitlement with a projection to the end of the contract period, and risks, technical debt, recommendations, and planned focus for the following month.

A task is considered delivered when deployed to production, verified against the agreed acceptance criteria, documented, and accepted by the requester. Certification of the monthly deliverable is contingent on receipt of a complete monthly report.

5. Qualifications & Skills

5.1 Education & Experience

  • University degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Software Engineering, or a related field.
  • At least three years of progressively responsible experience developing and supporting Salesforce solutions in complex enterprise environments.
  • Strong hands-on experience with Apex, Lightning Web Components, Flow, SOQL/SOSL, Salesforce configuration, security, APIs, testing, and deployment practices.
  • Experience with Salesforce Service Cloud, enterprise integrations, production support, and highly customized Salesforce environments.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple assigned tasks, maintain accurate work records, collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders, and deliver by agreed deadlines.
  • Direct experience with Agentforce IT Service is not required because the product is new. Experience with Agentforce, Einstein capabilities, ITSM processes, employee self-service, or knowledge management is desirable.

5.2 Technical Competencies

  • Development: Apex (classes, triggers, batch, queueable, scheduled), asynchronous patterns, governor limits, bulkification, SOQL/SOSL, Lightning Web Components, Aura and Visualforce (legacy maintenance), JavaScript ES6+, Flow, custom metadata, validation rules, Order of Execution
  • Service Cloud / ITSM: Case management, Omni-Channel routing, queues and skills-based assignment, entitlements, milestones and SLAs, knowledge management, service catalogue, CMDB and configuration items, ITIL incident / request / problem / change practices
  • AI and Agentforce: Agent topics and actions, prompt templates, grounding on knowledge and CMDB data, Einstein Trust Layer, agent testing and evaluation, escalation and human handoff design
  • Integration and DevOps: REST and SOAP APIs, Platform Events, Change Data Capture, External Services, Named Credentials, OAuth 2.0 / SAML, Microsoft Entra ID SSO, Microsoft Teams integration, middleware and iPaaS; Salesforce DX and CLI, sandboxes, Git and pull requests, CI/CD, static analysis, Apex unit testing and Jest
  • Security, Data, and Delivery: Profiles, permission sets and groups, sharing and visibility, field-level security, CRUD/FLS enforcement, SOQL injection prevention, event monitoring; data migration, quality tooling, reports and dashboards; Agile or Kanban working, backlog management, effort estimation, technical documentation

5.3 Certifications

Salesforce Certified Platform Developer is required or strongly preferred. Salesforce Administrator, Service Cloud Consultant, Platform App Builder, Platform Developer II, and Agentforce Specialist certifications are desirable.

6. Language Skills

English: Fluency in written and spoken English is required.

Other languages: Working knowledge of Spanish is desirable; knowledge of French or Portuguese is an asset.

7. Key Performance Indicators

  • Assigned tasks delivered by the agreed target date
    • Target: ≥ 90%
    • Measured: Monthly
  • Monthly report submitted complete and on time
    • Target: By 5th working day
    • Measured: Monthly
  • Critical (P1) regressions attributable to consultant-delivered changes
    • Target: Zero
    • Measured: Continuous
  • Apex unit test coverage on delivered code
    • Target: ≥ 85% org-wide
    • Measured: Per release
  • Security findings remediated in window; documentation and backlog current
    • Measured: 100%
    • Target: Monthly
  • Agent deflection / containment for in-scope service domains
    • Measured: Improving against baseline
    • Target: Monthly
  • Platform consumption within contracted entitlement
    • Measured: No unforecast overage
    • Target: Monthly

8. Work Schedule & Conditions

Position: Salesforce Developer Consultant

Work type/ Duty Station: Full-time consultancy; remote (off-site), with core hours overlapping Washington, D.C. business hours. Occasional mission travel may be required, subject to prior approval.

Duration: 6 months, extension subject to satisfactory performance, with a formal review in month three and availability of funds

Position Type: Band A of International PAHO Consultant (IPC-Band A)

Reporting To: Advisor, IT Operations — ITS

Remuneration: Daily rate $172

Confidentiality & IP: All PAHO projects, procurement, personnel, and Member State information shall be treated as confidential and shall comply with PAHO information security, data protection, and AI governance policies. All deliverables, templates, prompt libraries, agent and automation configurations, and work products are the property of PAHO.

ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • This vacancy notice may be used to identify candidates for other similar consultancies at the same level.
  • Successful candidates will be placed on the roster and subsequently may be selected for consultancy assignments falling in this area of work or for similar requirements/tasks/deliverables.  Inclusion in the Roster does not guarantee selection for a consultant contract.  There is no commitment on either side.
  • Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted.
  • All applicants are required to complete an on-line profile to be considered for this consultancy. For assessment of your application, please ensure that your profile in the PAHO Career page is updated; all experience records are entered with elaboration on tasks performed at the time.  Kindly note that CV/PHFs inserted via LinkedIn are no accessible.
  • A written test may be used as a form of screening.
  • If your candidature is retained for interview, you will be required to provide, in advance, a scanned copy of the degree(s)/diploma(s)/certificate(s) required for this position. PAHO/WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net/. PAHO will also use the databases of the Council for Higher Education Accreditation http://www.chea.org/search/default.asp and College Navigator, found on the website of the National Centre for Educational Statistics, https://nces.ed.gov/collegenavigator to support the validation process. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review.
  • Any appointment/extension of appointment is subject to PAHO/WHO Regulations, and e-Manual.
  • For information on PAHO please visit: http://www.paho.org
  • PAHO/WHO is committed to providing a respectful and supportive workplace for all personnel .
  • PAHO is an ethical organization that maintains high standards of integrity and accountability. People joining PAHO are required to maintain these standards both in their professional work and personal activities.
  • PAHO also promotes a work environment that is free from harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and other types of abusive behavior. PAHO conducts background checks and will not hire anyone who has a substantiated history of abusive conduct.
  • PAHO personnel interact frequently with people in the communities we serve. To protect these people, PAHO has zero tolerance for sexual exploitation and abuse. People who commit serious wrongdoings will be terminated and may also face criminal prosecution.
  • PAHO/WHO has a smoke-free environment and does not recruit smokers or users of any form of tobacco.
  • Applications from women and from nationals of non and underrepresented Member States are particularly encouraged.
  • Consultants shall perform the work as independent contractors in a personal capacity, and not as a representative of any entity or authority.  The execution of the work under a consultant contract does not create an employer/employee relationship between PAHO and the Consultant.
  • PAHO/WHO shall have no responsibility whatsoever for any taxes, duties, social security contributions or other contributions payable by the Consultant.  The Consultant shall be solely responsible for withholding and paying any taxes, duties, social security contributions and any other contributions which are applicable to the Consultant in each location/jurisdiction in which the work hereunder is performed, and the Consultant shall not be entitled to any reimbursement thereof by PAHO/WHO.

PURPOSE OF INTERNSHIP

INTRODUCTION
You are applying to the PAHO generic internship roster which is published twice a year and can be done in person or virtually. The roster will be made available to all PAHO offices from where direct contact will be made with suitable candidates only. In completing your profile, you will be able to choose up to 2 different work areas of interest.

OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME
The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) is the specialized international health agency for the Americas. It works with countries throughout the region to improve and protect people's health.

PAHO wears two institutional hats: it is the specialized health agency of the Inter-American System and also serves as Regional Office for the Americas of the World Health Organization (WHO), the specialized health agency of the United Nations. PAHO offers internships in our country - and regional offices, as well as at headquarters.

The PAHO internship program has three objectives:
a) to provide a framework for assigning students from diverse academic backgrounds to PAHO programs, where educational experience can be enhanced through practical work assignments;
b) to expose students to the work of PAHO and
c) to provide PAHO programs with the assistance of students specializing in various fields. Most students are placed in health-related programs, although placements in other area of work like for example communication, external relations, finance or human resources are also possible.

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES:

Under the supervision of a technical expert in the respective area, interns are assigned a project based on agreed terms of references and in line with their skills set. These terms of references typically include some or all of the following responsibilities:

  • review literature and conduct literature surveys
  • undertake web research and data collection on specific subject area organize data and documents
  • participate in the development of tools and guidelines
  • assist in drafting, formatting and editing policy briefs, tool kits, guides/manuals, hand-outs, brochures and reports
  • assist in organizing workshops, meetings, conferences, events
  • participate in on-going departmental projects

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Are in the final academic year of a bachelor's degree or enrolled in a master's or a doctoral program or have graduated within the last two years from a bachelor’s, master’s or doctoral program.

Skills

Core competencies

  • Team work
  • Respecting and promoting individual and cultural difference
  • Communication

All interns should be able to demonstrate the following skills in line with the WHO core competencies:

  • Communicating effectively orally and in writing
  • Showing willingness to learn from mistakes
  • Producing and delivering quality results
  • Working collaboratively with team member

In addition, interns need to be familiar with commonly used computer programs, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Knowledge of specialized computer programs, for example, statistical software such as XLStat may be an advantage.

Experience

Depending on the area of interest, the below experience may be needed and/or would be an advantage.

  • Experience in research and/or in drafting reports
  • Experience in the subject area through academic work or research
  • Field and/or developing country experience
  • Experience with data analysis, statistical packages and interest in the design of graphical display and analysis of health information in an international comparative perspective, such as for health system performance assessment
  • More specific experience such as specialized computer programs

Languages

Fluency in one of PAHO's working languages (reading, writing and speaking). PAHO official languages: English, Spanish, Portuguese and French. Knowledge of the local language in some duty stations can be an asset.

Age

Interns should be at least twenty years of age on the date of application.

Additional requirements:

  • are not related to a staff member as defined in Staff Rule 410.3 (i.e., spouse, children, parents, and siblings of the staff member or the children, parents, and siblings of the staff member’s spouse)
  • are not related to an individual who works for a national government or local authority (e.g. children or sibling of Ministry of Health personnel)
  • have not previously participated in PAHO's internship program.

Please note that internships at PAHO are very competitive and only a small number of applicants will be accepted every year. Only successful candidates will be contacted.

If selected for a PAHO Internship, you will be required to provide certified copies of proof of enrolment in a course of studies and a medical certificate of fitness for work.

  • Interviews are usually used as a form of screening.

  • We strongly recommend that candidates also upload a motivation letter in their application.

  • PAHO also promotes a work environment that is free from harassment, sexual harassment, discrimination, and other types of abusive behavior. PAHO conducts background checks and will not hire anyone who has a substantiated history of abusive conduct.
